subject: Science
title: Light and shadow
objectives: Children will notice that light comes from the sun and a torch.
Children will make and watch shadows.
content: Noticing light and dark, making shadows with the sun and a torch, and shadow puppets.
teachingActivities: Never let children look at the sun; use a torch with a firm cover and shine it on a wall; darken the room only as much as needed; stay close in dim light; use simple words.
learnerActivities: Say light or dark for a place, make a shadow and play with shadow puppets.
assessment: Observe whether each child says light or dark for a place and makes a shadow with a hand or toy.
expectedOutcomes: Says light or dark for a place.
Makes a shadow with a hand or toy.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: sun and sky

lessons.title: Light and dark
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will say if a place is light or dark.
successCriteria: Points to a source of light
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe movement and test objects with simple words.
resources: A picture of the sun and a lamp
lessons.starter: Switch off the room light a little and say "It is dark." Switch on a torch and say "Now there is light."
teacherActivities: Show a dark box and look inside. Shine a torch in and say "Light."
Show the sun and a lamp picture and say "They give us light."
Go to a bright place and a shaded place and say light and dark.
Ask "Where is it dark?" and "What gives light?"
learnerActivities: Children look inside and say dark and light.
Child points or says a word.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a dark box and look inside. Shine a torch in and say "Light." Children: Children look inside and say dark and light.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the sun and a lamp picture and say "They give us light." Children: Children point to the pictures.
Step 3. Teacher: Go to a bright place and a shaded place and say light and dark. Children: Child says light or dark.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Where is it dark?" and "What gives light?" Children: Child points or says a word.

practical.title: Light and dark
steps: Look inside a dark box or tent.
practical.safety: Stay close to children in dim light and never leave a child alone in a dark space. Do not shine a torch in anyone’s eyes.

differentiation.support: Look together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a dark place in the school.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Switch the lights back on and say "Light!"
lessons.homeConnection: Notice light and dark places at home with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say if a place is light or dark" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Light, light, shining bright. Dark, dark, nighttime.

lessons.title: Making shadows
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will make shadows with their bodies and objects.
successCriteria: Makes a shadow with a hand or toy
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe movement and test objects with simple words.
lessons.starter: Shine the torch on the wall and make a hand shadow. Say "Look, a shadow."
teacherActivities: Show a hand shadow on the wall and ask "What is this?"
Let each child hold their hand or a toy in front of the torch.
Move the toy closer and further and see the shadow change.
Go outside on a sunny day and look at shadows on the ground.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say big or small.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a hand shadow on the wall and ask "What is this?" Children: Children look and say shadow.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child hold their hand or a toy in front of the torch. Children: Child makes a shadow.
Step 3. Teacher: Move the toy closer and further and see the shadow change. Children: Children watch and say big or small.
Step 4. Teacher: Go outside on a sunny day and look at shadows on the ground. Children: Child looks at their shadow.

practical.title: Shadow play
steps: Shine a torch on a wall.
Make shadows with hands and toys.
Draw round a shadow with chalk outside.
practical.safety: Never look at the sun or shine a torch at eyes. Draw shadows with chalk on a safe paved area.

differentiation.support: Hold the toy together in front of the light.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a big and a small shadow.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you make a shadow?
questions.expected: Put something in front of the light.

lessons.conclusion: Switch off the torch and say "Goodbye, shadow."
lessons.homeConnection: Make hand shadows on a wall with a torch at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make shadows with their bodies and objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shadow puppets
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use shadow puppets to tell a short story.
successCriteria: Moves a puppet in front of the light
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe movement and test objects with simple words.
resources: Cardboard puppets on sticks: a bird, a cat, a fish
lessons.starter: Show a bird puppet in front of the torch and say "Look, a bird shadow on the wall."
teacherActivities: Move the puppets behind a sheet in front of the light.
Tell a short story with the puppets.
Let each child hold a puppet behind the sheet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Move the puppets behind a sheet in front of the light. Children: Children watch the shadows.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What animal is it?" Children: Child names the animal.
Step 3. Teacher: Tell a short story with the puppets. Children: Children listen and watch.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child hold a puppet behind the sheet. Children: Child moves the puppet.

practical.title: Shadow show
steps: Hang a sheet in front of a torch.
practical.safety: Secure the sheet firmly and keep cables out of reach. Use a battery torch only and stay close to children in the dim light.

differentiation.support: Hold the puppet together and move it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make up a short story for a puppet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Bow to the audience and put the puppets away.
lessons.homeConnection: Make shadow puppets at home with a torch and paper shapes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use shadow puppets to tell a short story" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shadows outside
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find shadows outside and see how they change.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe movement and test objects with simple words.
lessons.starter: Go outside on a sunny day and say "Where is your shadow? Can you find it?"
teacherActivities: Stand in the sun and look at your shadow.
Move and see the shadow move.
Draw round a friend’s shadow with chalk.
Stand in the shade and see that there is no shadow.
learnerActivities: Children move and watch their shadow.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Stand in the sun and look at your shadow. Children: Children look and say shadow.
Step 2. Teacher: Move and see the shadow move. Children: Children move and watch their shadow.
Step 3. Teacher: Draw round a friend’s shadow with chalk. Children: Child draws round a shadow.
Step 4. Teacher: Stand in the shade and see that there is no shadow. Children: Child notices the missing shadow.

practical.title: Shadow hunt
steps: Go to a sunny paved area.
Find and draw shadows with chalk.
practical.safety: Never look at the sun. Use hats, shade and water in hot weather and stay away from roads.

differentiation.support: Walk together and point to the shadow.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make their shadow tall and short.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is there a shadow in the shade?

expectedOutcomes: Notices that shadows move with them
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to your shadow and go inside.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for your shadow outside on a sunny day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find shadows outside and see how they change" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 light check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child describes light and makes shadows.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe movement and test objects with simple words.
lessons.starter: Sing the light and dark song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: light and dark, shadows and puppets.
At each station ask "Light or dark?" and "What makes a shadow?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: light and dark, shadows and puppets. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Light or dark?" and "What makes a shadow?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Light stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep children safe in dim light. Do not shine torches in eyes.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain shadows to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says light or dark; makes a shadow; names a source of light.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Switch off the torch and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about light and shadows at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child describes light and makes shadows" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
